title: Variables and core value types
body: Python names are bound to objects. Common built-in value types include integers, floating-point numbers, strings, booleans and None. A name can later be rebound to a different object.
source_title: Python Language Reference — Simple statements / assignment

title: Arithmetic, comparison and Boolean operators
body: Python provides arithmetic operators such as +, -, *, /, //, %, and **; comparison operators such as ==, !=, < and >; and Boolean operators `and`, `or` and `not`. Operator precedence affects evaluation order.

title: Conditional branching with if / elif / else
body: An `if` statement selects a suite based on the truth value of an expression. Additional conditions can be tested with `elif`, and `else` handles the remaining path.
source_title: Python Language Reference — The if statement

title: Mutable default argument behaviour
body: Default parameter expressions are evaluated when the function definition executes, not once per call. Reusing a mutable default can therefore share state between calls. A common pattern is to use None and create the mutable value inside the function.
source_title: Python Tutorial — More on Defining Functions

title: Exception handling
body: `try` statements can handle selected exceptions with `except` clauses and can include `else` and `finally`. Catching a specific exception type makes failure behaviour easier to reason about than indiscriminately catching every exception.
source_title: Python Language Reference — The try statement
